g: (slang, Australia) An official government car, especially a Comcar.
(genetics) The larger chromosome that has more genes, in the ZW system.
(statistics) The number of standard deviation units away from the mean a particular value of data lies.
A length of steel or aluminium with a Z-shaped cross-section.
The Z-shaped twist of yarn spun in a clockwise direction.
It's getting late: it's time to catch some z's.
A weighted average where the value for each component is weighted by the square of its mass or volume.

(algebraic geometry) The axis on a graph of at least three dimensions that is usually drawn vertically and usually shows the range of values of a variable dependent on two other variables or the third independent variable.
(construction) A steel bar consisting of a Z-shaped section.
A portable bed that folds into a Z shape.
A wire bend consisting of two consecutive 90° bends resembling the letter Z.
(particle physics) a fundamental particle, a gauge boson, that, together with the W-boson, mediates the weak nuclear force; it has a charge of 0
(computer graphics) A buffer for the purpose of tracking the relative depths of different objects in a scene and determining which are closer to the observer than others.
(computer graphics) The use of a z-buffer.
(UK) Any of the several early models of a police car.
(computer graphics) The elimination of certain objects from the display that should not be rendered because they are behind objects that are closer to the viewer.
(algebraic geometry) The direction aligned with the z-axis of a coordinate system.
(uncountable) A configuration of DNA in cells, left-hand twisting double helix, that takes up a zigzagging form due to the natural right-hand twisting tendency of DNA.
(countable) A DNA helix in such a configuration.
Any of a group of nonbenzodiazepine drugs with effects similar to benzodiazepines, used in the treatment of insomnia.

(computer graphics) A phenomenon in three-dimensional rendering where two or more primitives have similar values in the z-buffer, causing flickering as one is displayed varyingly behind or in front of the other.
(mathematics) A point at which a line crosses the z-axis of a Cartesian grid.
A group of people who are the furthest from stardom, unlike the A-list.
Someone on a Z-list; one who is very far from stardom.
(film) A very low-budget motion picture, especially one with poor production values.
(computer graphics) The order in which objects should be drawn in order to display correctly.
When you click on a window it is brought to the top of the z-order so that you can see it.
(computer graphics) A property of a graphical object that indicates its position in the z-order.
To get the rectangle to hide some of the text, make its z-order higher.
A package of six pills, each one containing 250 mg of the antibacterial azithromycin.
The pills in a Z-pak are to be taken as follows: […]
A kind of plasma confinement system that uses an electrical current in the plasma to generate a magnetic field that compresses it.
(surgery) A versatile plastic surgery technique involving a Z-shaped incision that is used to improve the functional and cosmetic appearance of scars.
(uncountable) A configuration of RNA, left-hand twisting double helix, that takes up a zigzagging form due to the natural right-hand twisting tendency of double-stranded RNA.
(countable) An RNA helix in such a configuration.
Shaped like the letter "Z" or its mirror image.
(statistics) Any statistical test for which the distribution of the test statistic under the null hypothesis can be approximated by a normal distribution.
(computer graphics) A comparison to determine which object should be at the front of the z-buffer.
(medicine, often attributive) A technique for intramuscular injection that uses a zigzag path.
(mathematics) A transform that converts a discrete time-domain signal into a complex frequency-domain representation.
(Unicode) A variant Han character, theoretically unifiable under the Han unification policy but encoded separately for backwards compatibility.
Any word starting with Z considered to be taboo in the given context, such as zipperhead, Zionist, zoophile, or zigger.
(Hebrew) Of blessed memory, may he/she/they rest in peace; used after a reference to one or more people who died.
Yitzhak Rabin (z"l) was a warrior turned peace-maker.
